title: Where registry providers serve from, and what they promise about data residency
note: Curated by the OpenNodes project from public sources (ONP-2 §3a, §3b). Each entry describes registry nodes (nodes) instead of creating its own listing. Sites in Canada, the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK are in the Canada and Europe seeds. documented = the provider's own dated page; claimed = provider statements, news or third-party reports. Residency is what the provider promises, with its source: processing (inference and stored data stay in scope), storage (data at rest only), none, unstated. Corrections by pull request.

residency.programme: Data Zone (US / EU) - EU Data Boundary
residency.statement: Data Zone deployments (Standard, Provisioned, Batch): processing only within the Microsoft-defined data zone. US = anywhere in the US; EU = Azure EU Data Boundary (EU plus EFTA such as Norway, Switzerland). Microsoft may add regions to a zone without notice.

Data Zone APAC: processing within the Asia Pacific data zone (currently covering regions in Australia, Japan, Korea, Singapore and India per the availability tables; Microsoft may add regions without notice).

Global deployment types (Global Standard, Global Provisioned, Global Batch, Developer) may process prompts in any Azure region where the model is deployed; Global Standard is Microsoft's recommended starting type.
Azure Government: USGov Data Zone deployments are processed only in US Gov Arizona or US Gov Virginia; Standard/Regional deployments in the deployment region; data at rest in the designated region.

providers.note: Runs on GPUs inside Cloudflare's network; a Sept 2024 press release claims GPUs in 180+ cities and inference close to the user, but no per-city list is published, so no sites are listed. Inputs/outputs are not retained after the request.

residency.statement: No processing-location promise: Workers AI is not compatible with Regional Services; Customer Metadata Boundary is supported, but it covers metadata, not prompts.

providers.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
providers.note: Proxy/gateway on Cloudflare's network forwarding to Workers AI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Replicate and other providers; optional logging and caching.

residency.statement: No location promise: AI Gateway is not compatible with Regional Services, and jurisdictional storage of logs is not supported yet.

providers.name: Hetzner Inference API (experimental)
providers.note: Experimental, free, OpenAI-compatible API (inference.hetzner.com/api/v1) serving Qwen models on Hetzner's own hardware in its data centres; which data centre is not stated (the experiments app's docs are behind login).

residency.statement: No location stated; Hetzner says it does not store request or response content, only usage metadata.

providers.name: Modal
providers.note: Serverless GPU platform running containers across several clouds; Modal Endpoints serve open models (shared or dedicated). Region codes (us, eu, ap, jp, uk, ...) are not mapped to cloud regions publicly. Inputs route through Virginia (us-east) by default, and payloads over 2 MiB go to object storage in us-east. Docs don't say where shared Endpoints run.

residency.statement: By default containers run globally across multiple clouds, with no location limit.
Functions can be pinned to a region (e.g. us, eu = EEA, ap, jp, uk) at a price multiplier; input routing can be set to us-east, us-west, eu-west or ap-south. Endpoints are not mentioned.

providers.name: Neon AI Gateway
providers.note: Gateway inside Neon projects in AWS us-east-2, us-east-1, eu-central-1 and ap-southeast-1; Neon says the models are hosted and powered by Databricks (see the Databricks entry). Docs don't say where inference runs relative to the project region.

residency.statement: No statement on where prompts are processed or stored.

providers.name: GitLab Duo
providers.note: GitLab.com/Dedicated use GitLab's AI gateway on Google Cloud (us-east4; europe-west2/3/9; asia-northeast1/3), forwarding to Anthropic, OpenAI (incl. via Amazon Bedrock), Google Vertex/Gemini and Fireworks-hosted models. GitLab picks the region, and models may be elsewhere. GitLab Duo Self-Hosted lets customers run the gateway and models in their own environment.

residency.statement: GitLab says the multi-region AI gateway is not a data residency solution; model locations are set by third-party providers and data may flow to other regions.

providers.name: SCNet (National Supercomputing Internet) Token Plan
providers.note: China's national supercomputing-internet platform, said in news reports to be run by Sugon Intelligent Computing; supports OpenAI/Anthropic protocols. Docs name no serving centre.

providers.name: Moore Threads KUAE Cloud

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.note: Data residency is set per project and needs sales approval. In-region inference exists only for the US, Europe (EEA + Switzerland) and the UAE; seven more regions store data at rest only. OpenAI does not name the facilities behind the regional endpoints. Abilene is the one serving site OpenAI names itself. Other announced Stargate sites (Shackelford County TX, Dona Ana County NM, Lordstown OH, Milam County TX, Michigan, Norway, UK) are left out: they are not confirmed as live or as serving API traffic.

sites.site: US regional processing (us.api.openai.com), facilities not named

sites.facility_operator: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (campus built by Crusoe)
sites.note: OpenAI says the site is 'training and serving' frontier systems. It does not say which API or ChatGPT traffic runs there.

sites.site: UAE regional processing (ae.api.openai.com), facilities not named
sites.note: In-region processing only for some models and snapshots (certain gpt-5.x on Chat Completions/Responses, text-embedding-3-large).

sites.facility_operator: G42 / Khazna, with Oracle, NVIDIA, Cisco, SoftBank
sites.note: First 200 MW was due in 2026; Abu Dhabi officials gave Q3 2026 for phase one (news reports). No confirmation found that it is live or that it backs ae.api.openai.com.

providers.models_note: Models are not tied to named sites. UAE processing covers only a short list of models; regional endpoints carry a 10% uplift for models released on or after 5 March 2026.

residency.statement: Projects without data residency have no processing constraint; content may be processed and stored wherever OpenAI runs the service.
US data-residency projects store customer content at rest and run inference in the US. Eligibility goes through sales.
Europe (EEA + Switzerland) projects store and process content in-region. Requires sales approval and ZDR, Modified Abuse Monitoring or a similar retention arrangement.
UAE projects store content at rest in the UAE and process in-region only for listed models and snapshots. Needs extra approval through sales.
Projects in Australia, Canada, Japan, India, Singapore, South Korea or the UK keep content at rest in-region, but inference may run, with temporary storage, outside the region.

providers.name: Anthropic (Claude API)
providers.note: Two controls: inference_geo ('global' by default, or 'us') sets where inference runs; workspace geo sets where data is stored and endpoint processing runs, and 'us' is the only value. Anthropic does not name the US facilities. Its $50B Fluidstack build (Texas, New York) is announced, not confirmed live. Colossus 1 (Memphis) is listed because Anthropic ties it to Claude serving capacity. Project Rainier (AWS, Indiana) and Google TPU capacity are left out: Anthropic does not say they serve API traffic in a given place.

sites.note: May 2026: Anthropic takes all of Colossus 1 (300+ MW, 220k+ NVIDIA GPUs) to add Claude capacity for usage limits and API rate limits. Anthropic does not name the city; Memphis is where xAI has publicly placed Colossus 1.

sites.site: Texas (custom data centre, city not named)
sites.note: Announced Nov 2025 to come online through 2026; no confirmation found that it serves traffic.

sites.site: New York (custom data centre, city not named)
sites.note: Announced Nov 2025 to come online through 2026; no confirmation found that it serves traffic.

residency.statement: Workspace geo 'us' (the only option) keeps data at rest and endpoint processing such as code execution in the US. With the default inference_geo 'global', inference may run in any geography.
Per request or as a workspace default, inference runs only on US infrastructure, at 1.1x token price. Also on Claude Platform on AWS and Anthropic-managed Google Cloud.

providers.name: Mistral AI (La Plateforme API)
providers.note: EU sites are already in eu:mistral. sites.site: US data centres behind api.us.mistral.ai (not named)

providers.models_note: Model availability differs by regional endpoint; Mistral says to call models.list on each.

residency.statement: Data is stored in the EU by default (in the US if you use the US endpoint). Some features may move data outside the EU temporarily, to subprocessors listed in the Trust Center.
Inference input and output are processed in data centres in EU and EFTA countries, at 1.1x price. The control plane (accounts, billing, analytics) is not regional.
Inference is processed in US data centres, at 1.1x price. The global api.mistral.ai endpoint has no committed inference location.

providers.name: Cohere
providers.note: Sites are already in ca:cohere (Google Cloud US-Central hosted API; Model Vault in Canada). No other sites found. import.hf.cohere is Hugging Face's router passing requests to the same Cohere API. Private, VPC and on-prem deployments run wherever the customer puts them.

residency.statement: The hosted platform runs on Google Cloud servers in US-Central; Cohere says it uses no servers outside the US and moves EU data to the US for processing.

providers.note: llama.developer.meta.com now redirects to dev.meta.ai: the Llama API became the Meta Model API (api.meta.ai; Muse models, SAM). No page found that states processing location, regions or hosting partners. The old Llama API data-commitments page now returns 404.

residency.statement: No public statement found on where API requests are processed or stored.

providers.name: Perplexity API (Sonar, Agent API)
providers.note: Sonar models are Perplexity's own. The Agent API also serves third-party models, which fall under those providers' terms, so for those it works as a router. residency.statement: No current statement on where API data is processed. ZDR is available only under a written agreement.

providers.name: AI21 Labs (AI21 Studio API)

providers.name: Reflection AI

providers.name: Poolside

providers.name: Arcee AI (Arcee Platform)

residency.statement: No statement on where prompts or outputs are processed or stored was found in the public docs or privacy policy.

providers.name: Agnes AI
providers.note: Hosted text, image, video and multimodal API (OpenAI-compatible); docs do not say whether it runs its own inference. Privacy page returned 404.

residency.statement: No statement on where prompts or outputs are processed or stored was found in the public docs or privacy policy.

providers.name: TrustedRouter
providers.note: Gateway to hundreds of models; its Trusted tier uses Tinfoil and Privatemode, and it offers an attested 'Europe West' gateway option (location not detailed). Gateway runs in a TEE with published attestation; privacy policy points to a subprocessor list that could not be read.

residency.statement: Privacy policy says TrustedRouter and its providers may process information in the US and other countries; regions and provider routes differ and customers must use route controls to pin them. Prompt/output logs are said not to be kept.

providers.name: TokenGo
providers.note: Model routing service operating on its own infrastructure plus unnamed datacentre partners, with official provider APIs as fallback. No countries or hosting providers named.

residency.statement: Policy says the company operates globally and data may be processed outside the user's country (SCCs for transfers); no countries are named. Enterprise customers can enable zero-retention routing on supported models.

providers.name: Modelis
providers.note: OpenAI-compatible gateway to about 95 text models from providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI and DeepSeek; upstreams not specifically named in policy.

residency.statement: Policy says data may be processed in countries other than the user's, including by upstream providers; no countries listed.

providers.name: DaoXE
providers.note: API gateway and distribution platform (OpenAI/Claude/Gemini-compatible) per its title; nothing on upstreams or data location in reachable pages.

residency.statement: No statement on where prompts or outputs are processed or stored was found in the public docs or privacy policy.

providers.name: engy
providers.note: Open GPU network: requests go to a worker run by engy or an independent operator; some workers use confidential computing. Worker countries not stated, so no sites. Edge via Cloudflare.

residency.statement: Prompts and outputs are not stored by the gateway; a ZDR flag restricts routing to confidential-compute or engy-operated workers. Worker locations and countries are not stated.

providers.name: Claudinio
providers.note: Flat-rate subscription to two coding models (Claudinio, Claudius); does not say who serves them.

residency.statement: Says prompts and responses are never stored (only anonymous usage metadata); processing location not stated.

providers.name: FreeModel
providers.note: Tagline 'One API for every frontier model' suggests a gateway; nothing on upstreams or data location found.

residency.statement: No statement on where prompts or outputs are processed or stored was found in the public docs or privacy policy.

providers.name: QVAC (Tether)
providers.note: Open-source SDK (launched April 2026) for running models on user devices, based on a llama.cpp fork, with P2P model distribution. The npm page returned 403; evidence is press coverage of the vendor's claims.

providers.name: OpenReason
providers.note: Not an inference provider: a team analytics tool that receives telemetry from Claude Code, Codex and Cursor; requests still go directly to Anthropic and OpenAI. Telemetry storage location not stated.

residency.statement: No statement on where prompts or outputs are processed or stored was found in the public docs or privacy policy.

providers.name: Hopper
providers.note: Serves a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model through an OpenAI-compatible API; does not say who runs it.

residency.statement: No statement on where prompts or outputs are processed or stored was found in the public docs or privacy policy.

providers.name: Aixy
providers.note: AI gateway (OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible, also self-hostable) that routes to provider-qualified models. Its own gateway infrastructure is in AWS Frankfurt (EU seed scope, not listed as a site); upstream model providers may process elsewhere.

residency.statement: Aixy-operated infrastructure is hosted on AWS Europe (Frankfurt) and database backups expire after seven days. Model providers chosen by the customer may process requests in other locations; non-EEA transfers need safeguards.
